supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:46, ivy.chen ran PowerShell from Explorer to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon then recorded creation of that archive.
At 13:45:32, ivy.chen launched Chrome from Explorer directly to quickshare-drop.net.

The proxy recorded a successful HTTPS tunnel to quickshare-drop.net with 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes and 8,800 server-to-client bytes; Zeek recorded approximately 51 MB sent over the same workstation-to-proxy connection, initiated by Chrome.

The close timing between creating an archive of the Clients share and sending tens of megabytes through a browser tunnel to an unapproved file-sharing destination strongly supports attempted or completed unauthorized data exfiltration.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy record identifies the tunnel destination and byte counts, but the evidence does not show the HTTPS request path, payload, or server-side receipt.
The archive creation record does not establish the archive's contents, size, or whether that exact file was uploaded.
The evidence links the archive creation and large browser transfer by user, host, and timing, but does not directly identify the transferred bytes as c.zip.
claims_not_established: Whether the transfer completed successfully or the destination retained the data.
Whether c.zip was the uploaded object or what specific client data it contained.
Whether ivy.chen had authorization or a legitimate business reason for this transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine c.zip, including its hash, size, contents, and creation metadata.
Collect file-access auditing or server-side records for \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients around 13:39 UTC.
Obtain detailed proxy or endpoint network records that could identify the HTTPS upload request, payload size, and completion status; seek destination-side records if available.
Confirm the transfer's business purpose and authorization with the data owner and ivy.chen.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect vpnui.exe was launched by ivy.chen at 14:04:55; this record shows a process launch, not an established VPN connection. Review separately against the environment's remote-access policy. (T039-00190, T039-00191)
